goals: Tell a concave mirror from a convex one
Use pole, centre of curvature, focus and focal length
Say where each mirror is used

cards.title: Two kinds of spherical mirror
cards.body:
A spherical mirror is part of a hollow sphere.
- **Concave**: the shiny side curves inwards, like the inside of a spoon.
- **Convex**: the shiny side bulges outwards, like the back of a spoon.

rows.value: The centre of the mirror's surface
The centre of the sphere the mirror is part of
The distance from P to C
Where rays parallel to the axis meet, or seem to come from
The distance from P to F

cards.question: A spherical mirror has a radius of curvature of 20 cm. What is its focal length?
cards.why: The focus lies halfway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so f = R/2 = 20/2 = 10 cm.

cards.title: Concave mirrors bring light together
cards.body:
Rays parallel to the principal axis reflect off a concave mirror and meet at the principal focus F, in front of the mirror.

That's why a concave mirror is called a **converging** mirror.

cards.title: Convex mirrors spread light out
cards.body:
Parallel rays reflect off a convex mirror and spread out. Traced backwards, they seem to come from a focus F **behind** the mirror.

That's why a convex mirror is called a **diverging** mirror.

cards.question: Which mirror is used as the rear-view mirror in vehicles?
cards.why: A convex mirror always gives an erect, smaller image and shows a much wider view than a plane mirror, so the driver sees more of the road behind.

rows.value: Real, inverted, smaller, between F and C
Real, inverted, same size, at C
Virtual, erect, larger, behind the mirror

cards.title: Concave mirrors at work
cards.body:
- **Shaving and make-up mirrors** and **dentists' mirrors**: held close, they give a larger, erect image.
- **Torches and car headlights**: a bulb at F sends out a parallel beam.
- **Solar furnaces**: they bring sunlight together at one point to make heat.

cards.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror to get a virtual, erect and magnified image?
cards.why: Only when the object is between the focus and the pole do the reflected rays spread out. They seem to meet behind the mirror, which gives a virtual, erect, magnified image, like a make-up mirror held close.

points: Concave mirrors converge light; convex mirrors diverge it
Convex: rear-view mirrors. Concave: make-up mirrors, torches, solar furnaces
